The session turned the CI supply-chain check green again: the cargo-deny advisory ignore list gains a fourth id, RUSTSEC-2026-0543 (chrono unmaintained, no safe upgrade), on a second ground, an unmaintained upstream, beside the first ground for the rmcp advisories.
It ends every booted end-to-end test process with its test: the in-test harness boot's stamping viola verify now gets SIGTERM when its test thread ends (it was SIGKILL), and the supervisor still gets SIGKILL.
It added two integration tests: a killed test leaves no stamping verify behind (checked by process, run-dir and stamp reads), and a census finding no untied boot in the e2e crate's tests. The in-test boots of the harness lifecycle and e2e cli tests are now tied.
The shared source-scan masker's 14-row rstest table is now one test over a labelled case table, so the coverage count fell from 3510 to 3462 with the cases themselves unchanged. No product code, command output, status shape, log format, dependency or spec master changed.
CI on the pre-CI commit read green with 7 of 7 checks, supply-chain among them; pre-push gate breaches none. The longest harness lifecycle case takes 20.6 s against a 20 s CI kill line. That finding goes to route-resolve and is not amended here.

body: decision/a11y-ci-github-actions: the push/PR workflow's supply-chain check went from red to green (7 of 7 checks green). Nothing about the a11y checks in that workflow changed.
decision/ci-test-gate-no-skips: three integration tests were added, all running and none skipped. The test gate still allows no skips.
decision/zero-flakiness: the new kill-witness and census tests wait under a fixed bound with no retries. Their wait now needs verify to be mid-run inside its own run dir.

decision/a11y-cases-inside-coverage-suite: the coverage suite's passed count fell from 3510 to 3462 because one table of shared-helper cases collapsed into one test. No a11y case was added or removed.

decision/a11y-failures-are-nextest-failures: indirectly, through the nextest CI kill-line finding. The harness lifecycle readiness-timeout case runs 20.6 s against the 20 s ci kill line. That finding is placed at route-resolve, not here.
decision/gate-requires-coverage-doctest and decision/a11y-gate-breach-fails-build: the pre-push coverage run read green with gate breaches none, at the new passed count.

The tied test verify now ends by TERM, which takes verify's stopped path, so it removes its own run dirs and writes no stamp. The verify output and exit contracts are unchanged.
decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver: indirectly. The test harness's new waits are bounded on the test driver, never on a human.
decision/mutation-audit-covers-crate-invariants: indirectly. The shared masker's own cases now run as one labelled-table test in every test binary that takes it, the e2e crate's included.

CLI refusal, fault and --json failure contracts, and exit codes 2, 10, 11, 13, 14, 20 and 21. No refusal word, hint, code word or exit code changed.

Cognitive accessibility decisions (fixed CLI strings pinned by literal, one hint per code, errors as word, detail and hint). No fixed CLI copy changed.

viola revive, link/unlink, plugin install, hook call, MCP frame tool and frame verb refusal contracts. No product command changed.

The new ignore stands on a second, widened ground: an unmaintained upstream with no safe upgrade, admitted on the founder's word, re-read at each epoch boundary; the list's comment now states both grounds (the first is the rmcp advisory response). Every in-test boot in viola-e2e's lifecycle and CLI tests is now tied, held by a new census over viola-e2e's tests; a new kill witness proves a killed test leaves no stamping verify, no probe dir and no stamp written.
The shared source-scan masker's own cases became one labelled-table test so viola-e2e, which has no rstest, can take it; no dependency added, CI green on all seven checks.

body_fields.because: The shared source-scan masker's rstest table failed to compile in viola-e2e and became a plain case table, a convention binding every helper taken by path.

body_fields.what: one entry of the advisory ignore list, held id by id with its reason in deny.toml and in security-plan's ignore row; architecture keeps only the grounds an ignore may stand on.

body_fields.why: The advisory ignore list no longer holds exactly the three disabled-rmcp-feature ids: it holds four, the fourth on the unmaintained-upstream ground, so a row keyed and named for the rmcp ignores alone no longer states the list.
body_fields.because: The ignore list moved from three ids to four with RUSTSEC-2026-0543, so the row naming exactly three is false and its heir states the whole list.

body_fields.name: Advisory ignores admitted on two grounds only
body_fields.rule: An advisory ignore stands on one of two grounds: the Critical CVE response to an advisory confined to a disabled feature, or an unmaintained advisory with no safe upgrade whose crate an upstream dependency brings into the graph; each carries its reason beside it.
body_fields.why: The second ground widens the Critical CVE response; each unmaintained-upstream ignore is re-read at every epoch boundary, its only control.
body_fields.because: The advisory rule was widened from the disabled-feature response alone to a second, unmaintained-upstream ground, and no standing row states the rule with both grounds.

body_fields.name: Closed advisory ignore list
body_fields.rule: cargo-deny treats unmaintained and unsound advisories as failures, denies yanked crates and ignores exactly RUSTSEC-2026-0457, RUSTSEC-2026-0461 and RUSTSEC-2026-0462, each in an rmcp feature banned or off in the release graph, and RUSTSEC-2026-0543, chrono unmaintained with no safe upgrade.
body_fields.why: The rmcp ids stand under the Critical CVE response until rmcp leaves its below-3.5 range; the chrono id stands on the unmaintained-upstream ground, re-read at each epoch boundary.
body_fields.because: The ignore list now holds four ids, the fourth on the unmaintained-upstream ground, and replaces the row that named exactly the three rmcp ids.

body_fields.value: The root binary takes chrono directly, without default features, for the millisecond UTC timestamp, and keeps it though unmaintained: RUSTSEC-2026-0543 stands in the cargo deny ignore list on the unmaintained-upstream ground, re-read at each epoch boundary; jiff and time are not adopted.
body_fields.because: The direct chrono dependency now stands under an admitted unmaintained advisory with no patched version, so the row that decides chrono is taken must say it is kept on that ground and its alternatives not adopted.

body_fields.why: The advisory ignore list no longer holds exactly the three disabled-rmcp-feature ids: it holds four, the fourth on the unmaintained-upstream ground, so a row keyed and named for the rmcp ignores alone no longer states the list.
body_fields.because: The ignore list moved from three ids to four with RUSTSEC-2026-0543, so the row naming exactly three is false and its heir states the whole list.

body_fields.name: Advisory ignores admitted on two grounds only
body_fields.rule: An advisory ignore is admitted only as the Critical CVE response for a disabled rmcp feature or for an unmaintained upstream with no safe upgrade; each entry carries its reason, the comment over the list states both grounds, and each unmaintained-upstream ignore is re-read at every epoch boundary.
body_fields.because: The advisory rule was widened from the disabled-feature response alone to a second, unmaintained-upstream ground, and no standing row states the rule with both grounds.

body_fields.rule: cargo-deny treats unmaintained and unsound advisories as failures, denies yanked crates and ignores exactly RUSTSEC-2026-0457, RUSTSEC-2026-0461 and RUSTSEC-2026-0462, for rmcp features banned or off in the release graph, and RUSTSEC-2026-0543, chrono unmaintained with no safe upgrade.
body_fields.why: The three rmcp ids stand under the Critical CVE response for a disabled feature, the chrono id under the unmaintained-upstream ground.
body_fields.because: The ignore list now holds four ids, the fourth on the unmaintained-upstream ground, and replaces the row that named exactly the three rmcp ids.

body_fields.relied: A stopped viola verify's own guard ends its children, removes its own run dirs and writes no stamp, which the probe-directory cleanup rows already state; the test harness's parent-death tie that makes a killed test stop verify by SIGTERM is how the e2e harness is built, held by the code and test-plan's harness row.

body_fields.value: Ignored with a reason: an advisory only in an rmcp feature banned or off in the release graph, until rmcp leaves <3.5; an unmaintained-upstream advisory with no safe upgrade, re-read each epoch.
body_fields.because: The ignore list gains RUSTSEC-2026-0543 on the unmaintained-upstream ground, so the exception now holds two grounds, not only the rmcp one.

body_fields.value: Ignored with a reason: an advisory only in an rmcp feature banned or off in the release graph, until rmcp leaves <3.5; an unmaintained-upstream advisory with no safe upgrade, re-read each epoch.
body_fields.because: The ignore list gains RUSTSEC-2026-0543 on the unmaintained-upstream ground, so the exception now holds two grounds, not only the rmcp one.

body_fields.value: The supervisor is spawned as an ordinary child with no detach flags and outlives boot; the agent-run CLI boot leaves it untied, stopping only through its stop request, while an in-test harness session ties it to the test thread by parent-death SIGKILL and its stamping viola verify by SIGTERM.
body_fields.because: The in-test boot's tied stamping verify now takes SIGTERM at its test thread's end while the supervisor keeps SIGKILL, so one parent-death kill for both is no longer true.

body_fields.value: viola-e2e and viola-core carry no rstest dev-dependency; their table-driven cases, and the own cases of a shared helper taken by path, which run in every taker, are labelled tables in one test.
body_fields.because: A shared helper taken by path carries its own cases into every taker, viola-e2e among them, so its cases join the exception to rstest case tables.

body_fields.name: No viola-e2e test boots a harness session untied
body_fields.rule: No viola-e2e test boots a harness session untied: a census over viola-e2e's test sources finds every in-test boot tied, and is read red on a planted untied boot first.
body_fields.because: The chunk ties every in-test boot and adds a census proven on a planted positive, a rule the root-only untied-spawn row does not cover.

body_fields.name: Kill witness for a tied stamping verify
body_fields.rule: A kill witness for a tied stamping verify waits until verify holds a child inside a viola-verify run dir, asserts an owned dir stood at the kill, and reads the stamp's absence besides processes and dirs.
body_fields.why: An untied verify orphaned by the kill finishes inside the wait bound and removes its own dirs, so processes and dirs alone cannot tell it from a tied one.
body_fields.because: Measurement showed a process-and-dir witness cannot separate a tied verify from an untied one, so the witness design is a decision future kill witnesses must keep.

body:
The supply-chain gate reads green again: the cargo-deny advisory ignore list widened from three ids to four, adding RUSTSEC-2026-0543 (chrono unmaintained, no patched version) on a second ground, the founder's unmaintained-upstream ground of 2026-11-17, its entry carrying its reason and a re-read at each epoch boundary.
The comment above the ignore list now states both grounds: the disabled-feature rmcp advisories and the unmaintained upstream with no safe upgrade. Bans, licences, sources and the graph are unchanged; no dependency, lockfile or tool version moved.
The fuzz workspace's own advisory audit now prints four advisory-not-detected warnings, up from three, and still passes.
Test-only: the e2e harness's in-test boot now ties its stamping viola verify to the test thread by a parent-death SIGTERM, up from SIGKILL, so verify's own guard ends its children and removes its own run dirs when a test is killed. The supervisor keeps its parent-death SIGKILL.
Two tests were added: a killed-test witness that no stamping verify, run dir or stamp outlives its test, and a census that no in-test boot in the e2e crate goes untied. The shared source masker's case table became one labelled test, with no rstest dev-dependency added.
CI went green on all 7 checks, supply-chain among them. No product symbol, command, status shape, log format or contract changed.

body_fields.what: the cargo-deny configuration of the root graph: the advisory ignore list with each id's reason and the comment stating its grounds, beside the bans, the licence allow list and the crates.io-only sources
the e2e test harness's in-test boot, which ties the supervisor and its stamping viola verify to the test thread by a parent-death signal (verify now SIGTERM, supervisor SIGKILL)
the e2e harness lifecycle tests, whose in-test boots now pass tied
the e2e crate's CLI tests driving a booted session, whose in-test boot now passes tied

the killed-test process hygiene tests: a killed test leaves no harness session and no stamping verify, its run dirs or a stamp, and a census that no in-test boot goes untied; test-side removal of the victim's own leftover dirs only
the one shared source masker the census tests take, blanking comments and strings before a census scans code; its own cases now run as one labelled table test

body: decision/rmcp-advisory-ignores holds that the ignore list is exactly RUSTSEC-2026-0457, RUSTSEC-2026-0461 and RUSTSEC-2026-0462 on the disabled-rmcp-feature ground alone. It is now stale: there are four ids and a second ground.

The Dependency Security rule that an advisory may be ignored only as the Critical CVE response for a disabled feature is widened by the unmaintained-upstream ground. decision/cve-sla-disabled-feature and decision/cve-sla-enabled-feature still hold for the first ground, but the new ground's row belongs beside them.

decision/cargo-deny-gate, decision/ci-cargo-deny-gate and decision/cargo-deny-audit: the root-graph cargo-deny gate went from red on RUSTSEC-2026-0543 back to green. It went green by an admitted ignore, not by an upgrade.

decision/fuzz-lockfile-own-audit, decision/fuzz-lockfile-audited-separately and the fuzz workspace exemption rows: the fuzz lockfile's own advisory audit now carries four advisory-not-detected warnings, up from three. Touch any row whose cell counts those warnings or names the ignored ids.

decision/scheduled-advisory-run and decision/manual-dependency-updates: the new ignore is to be re-read at each epoch boundary, with Epoch 4's boundary named. It is a standing review cadence for one ignore.

decision/exact-dependency-pins and decision/exact-third-party-pins: chrono comes in through rmcp 3.4.1 and schemars 1.2.2 via the MCP crate, beside viola's and viola-state's own use. No safe upgrade exists and no pin moved.

decision/verify-probe-dirs-cleanup and decision/verify-probes-confined-to-own-dir: verify's Run A OS-temp dir is removed by its own guard on pass, fail, Ctrl-C or TERM; SIGKILL, a crash or a failed handler install leave it for removal by hand. Booted tests now take the TERM path, and a killed-test witness reads that the dirs are gone.

decision/e2e-home-removal-own-dirs-only and decision/test-removal-own-dirs-only: the new killed-test witness removes only the victim's own leftover home and run dirs. Two empty verify dirs left by SIGKILL control firings were removed by hand.
decision/tests-use-own-home and decision/test-homes-gitignored: the new witness boots its victim in its own scratch home under the OS temp dir.
decision/bounded-readers-census and the other census rules: the census tests share one source masker, not a copy, and the e2e crate now takes that one masker for its untied-boot census.
decision/stamps-written-only-by-verify: the killed-test witness reads that a stopped verify writes no stamps file, because verify returns interrupted before updating stamps.

body_fields.fact: An advisory ignore is admitted on one of two grounds only: the Critical CVE response for a disabled rmcp feature, or an unmaintained upstream with no safe upgrade (the founder's ground of 2026-11-17). Each ignore entry carries its reason, the comment over the list states both grounds, and each unmaintained-upstream ignore is re-read at every epoch boundary.

The advisory ignore list holds exactly four ids: RUSTSEC-2026-0457, RUSTSEC-2026-0461 and RUSTSEC-2026-0462 for disabled rmcp features, and RUSTSEC-2026-0543 (chrono unmaintained, brought in by rmcp and schemars through the MCP crate beside viola's and viola-state's own use) on the unmaintained-upstream ground. RUSTSEC-2026-0543 is to be re-read at Epoch 4's boundary.

A test-booted stamping viola verify is tied to its test thread by a parent-death SIGTERM, and the supervisor by SIGKILL. A killed test therefore lets verify's own guard end its children and remove its run dirs, and verify writes no stamp.

body: Authentication and authorization: the peer euid checks, the socket directory and mode checks, the strict-modes checks and their refusal contracts are unchanged. No product code changed.
Input validation: frame caps, paste text character sets, hook and MCP input checks, the name type and the validators in the core crate are untouched.
Error handling and every product contract: CLI exit codes, channel methods and errors, MCP tool results, refusal words and log lines are unchanged.
Secret management: the credential strip, the hermetic pre-push environment, the canary scan classes and the live rig's credential handling are untouched.
The threat model's absences: no network listener, outbound call, release stage or secret store was added.
CI workflow rows: action SHA pins, least workflow permissions, zizmor, toolchain and MSRV pins, and the release build's test-feature refusal are unchanged. No workflow or tool version moved.
Data protection's fixture hygiene, plugin file rewriting, pinned-binary hashing and log modes are untouched.

The supply-chain gate reads green again: the cargo-deny advisory ignore list gains RUSTSEC-2026-0543 (chrono unmaintained, no patched version, brought in by rmcp and schemars through viola-mcp), admitted on a second ground, an unmaintained upstream with no safe upgrade, on the founder's word, re-read at each epoch boundary; the list goes from three ids to four and the comment above it states both grounds.
Every booted viola-e2e test process now ends with its test: the in-test boot's tied stamping viola verify takes SIGTERM at its test thread's end, so verify's own stop ends its children and removes its own run dirs, while the supervisor keeps SIGKILL.
The in-test boots of viola-e2e's harness lifecycle and CLI tests are now tied, held by a new census over viola-e2e's test sources that finds no untied boot (planted positive first).
A new kill witness proves a killed test leaves no stamping verify: process and dir reads alone could not separate a tied verify from an untied one (an orphaned untied verify finishes inside the wait bound and removes its dirs), so the witness also reads the stamp's absence and waits until verify holds a child inside a viola-verify run dir.
The one shared source-scan masker, taken by path, now also serves viola-e2e; its 14 cases became a labelled table in one plain test instead of rstest cases, since viola-e2e takes no rstest; the test count moved 3510 to 3462 by that alone (cases unchanged).
CI on the pre-CI commit reads green, 7 of 7 checks, supply-chain among them; no product symbol, command, status shape, log format or dependency changed.

body_fields.what: the cargo-deny supply-chain gate's policy — the advisory ignore list with each entry's reason, the bans, licences, sources and graph settings
viola-e2e's in-test boot of a harness session — makes the home, runs the stamping viola verify and starts the supervisor, tying each to the test thread by a parent-death signal
viola-e2e's harness lifecycle tests — boot, readiness timeout and supervisor stop of a booted session, each boot now tied
viola-e2e's harness CLI tests — status, logs and cleanup driving a booted session, each boot now tied
viola-e2e's tied-children kill witnesses — a killed test leaves no harness session and no stamping verify, and the census that finds no untied in-test boot

the one shared source-scan masker taken by path by the root census binaries (bounded readers, error bodies, OS-gated tests, killed-test cross) and now by viola-e2e's tied-children tests, with its own masking cases

body: decision/no-advisory-ignored (section 1): its exception holds only the rmcp ground; it now takes the second ground, an unmaintained upstream with no patched version and no safe upgrade, admitted on the founder's word, its reason on the entry and re-read at each epoch boundary (RUSTSEC-2026-0543, chrono).

decision/no-ignored-advisories (section 9): the same second ground joins its exception; any cell naming exactly three ignored ids now holds four (RUSTSEC-2026-0457, RUSTSEC-2026-0461, RUSTSEC-2026-0462, RUSTSEC-2026-0543).
Any row whose cell holds the advisory ignore list's ids or its count (three) is stale: the list is now four ids.

Indirect, through the gate policy: decision/cargo-deny-gate, decision/cargo-deny-supply-chain-gate, decision/supply-chain-ci-gates and decision/supply-chain-fail-closed rule over the supply-chain gate whose advisory list widened; the gate stays fail-closed and reads green with the widened list.

decision/weekly-advisories-run and decision/weekly-advisory-scan: the fuzz workspace's advisory audit now reports four advisory-not-detected warnings, not three; a touch only where a row's cell holds that count.

decision/supervisor-ordinary-child: it says the in-test boot ties the supervisor and its stamping viola verify to the test thread by a parent-death kill; now the stamping verify takes SIGTERM and only the supervisor takes SIGKILL.
decision/tied-child-spawn-thread: the tied children are still spawned on a thread that outlives them; true of either signal, but its wording may name the kill signal of the stamping verify.
decision/no-untied-viola-spawn: the root-test rule now has a viola-e2e counterpart, a census that finds no untied in-test boot in viola-e2e's test sources.

decision/rstest-case-tables: an exception — the shared masker's cases, carried by path into every taker, are a labelled table in one plain test, since viola-e2e takes no rstest and adds no dev-dependency.
decision/one-shared-test-helper and decision/shared-e2e-helpers: the one masker stays the single copy and gains viola-e2e as a taker; no census defines its own copy.
decision/bounded-remove-the-guard-witness: a new kill witness with its controls (verify given SIGKILL again, verify untied, census blinded) reads red under each and green as shipped.
contract/verify-stop/signal (SIGINT or SIGTERM): the tied stamping verify now relies on verify's own SIGTERM stop to end its children and remove its run dirs; a stopped verify writes no stamp.

decision/stamps-written-only-by-verify, decision/verify-sole-stamp-writer and decision/one-verify-stamp-per-build: the witness reads the stamp file's absence after the kill, relying on an interrupted verify never writing stamps.
decision/within-7s-wait-bound: every new wait of the witness and census sits under WITHIN.
decision/killed-test-child-uninstrumented: the new witness spawns a victim test entry that is killed mid-stamp, a killed test child of this kind.

decision/verify-driven-tests-20s-kill and decision/ci-stamped-home-kill-line: viola-e2e's lifecycle, CLI and tied-children tests drive a stamping verify through the boot; measured slowest cases 20.644 s (the readiness-timeout case, waiting out the 20 s readiness deadline), 5.991 s and 1.014 s, so a 20 s kill line would kill the lifecycle binary's readiness-timeout case; the finding's placement is the route's, not amended by this session.
decision/stamping-verify-passes-transcript: the stamping verify the boot runs still gets its transcript; only its parent-death signal changed.

body_fields.fact: No viola-e2e test boots a harness session untied: a census over viola-e2e's test sources finds every in-test boot tied, read red on a planted untied boot first.

A kill witness for a tied stamping verify waits until verify holds a child inside a viola-verify run dir, asserts an owned dir stood at the kill, and reads the stamp's absence besides processes and dirs, since an untied verify orphaned by the kill finishes inside the wait bound and removes its own dirs.
A shared test helper taken by path carries its own cases into every taker, so its cases are a labelled table in one plain test, never rstest cases, as the E2E crate takes no rstest.
